facts.icd10_text: Age-related osteoporosis with current pathological fracture, vertebra(e), initial encounter

statements.text: Back pain began 07/24/2026 after a fall from standing height, 8 weeks before this visit.
MRI thoracolumbar spine 09/06/2026: acute osteoporotic L2 compression fracture with bone marrow edema on STIR imaging.
Seen in the outpatient spine clinic; not hospitalized for this fracture.
Pain NRS 7/10 despite 7 weeks of optimal non-surgical management with oxycodone 5 mg as needed, a thoracolumbar brace and activity modification.
Pain has worsened over the past two weeks despite bracing.
Referred for DEXA bone density testing and osteoporosis education; enrolled in the osteoporosis treatment program.
Back pain localizes to the fractured level; afebrile with no signs of infection or discitis.

Primary Care Progress Note
Date: 07/31/2026
Patient: Simone Glover, 80-year-old female

Subjective:
Ms. Glover presents for her routine follow-up. She reports no new complaints today and feels generally well. She denies any recent falls or injuries.

Objective:
Vital signs are stable and within normal limits. Physical examination reveals no acute distress. Cardiovascular, respiratory, and abdominal exams are unremarkable. Musculoskeletal exam shows no tenderness or swelling.

Assessment:
Ms. Glover is an 80-year-old female with no new issues at this visit. She remains stable.

Plan:
Continue current management and routine monitoring. Encourage regular physical activity and balanced nutrition. Follow up in 6 months or sooner if any concerns arise.

Radiology Report
Date: 09/06/2026
Patient: Simone Glover, 80-year-old female

Examination: MRI thoracolumbar spine

Findings:
MRI thoracolumbar spine 09/06/2026: acute osteoporotic L2 compression fracture with bone marrow edema on STIR imaging.

Impression:
There is an acute osteoporotic compression fracture at the L2 vertebral body, demonstrated by bone marrow edema on STIR sequences. No other acute abnormalities are identified.

Recommendations:
Clinical correlation is advised. Further management should consider the patient's overall clinical status and osteoporosis treatment.

Spine Intervention Consultation

Patient: Simone Glover, 80-year-old female

History:

Pain NRS 7/10 despite 7 weeks of optimal non-surgical management with oxycodone 5 mg as needed, a thoracolumbar brace and activity modification. Pain has worsened over the past two weeks despite bracing.

Examination:

Plan:
